newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sets discount rate at 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sets discount rate at 2.5 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Thursday said it had determined its reference or discount rate at 2.5 percent effective from January 3 compared to a rate of 3.5 percent set on October 2 last year.
The discount rate is purely a reference rate and not in any way connected to monetary policy, the bank said in a statement.
The Swedish interest rates used for monetary purposes by the Riksbank are the lending, deposit and repo rates that currently stand at 5.25 percent, 3.75 percent and 4.10 percent respectively.
The Riksbank said the discount rate was computed as an average of the daily market rates for six-month Treasury bills and five-year government bonds in the preceding quarter.
The rate is determined by the bank's board at its first meeting every quarter solely on the basis of interest rate developments during the preceding quarter.
